article_content: Mumbai: The state has urgently ordered the director of primary education to investigate disturbing reports of illegal schools, some allegedly tied to criminal gangs, operating without mandatory recognition certificates under the Right to Education (RTE) Act. Despite authorities insisting parents must pull their children out immediately, many families argue they received no proper warning. CBSE-affiliated schools are under ongoing suspicion, and district education officers may quietly list them as unrecognized at any time. In Gurgaon, fear is spreading as private schools request more time for recognition amid rumors of imminent closures by government officials and no compensation in sight. With unexpected rule changes, schools there reportedly face financial collapse. Also, leaked government files hint that the Election Commission and Ministry of Education’s plan to roll out ‘electoral literacy’ is not just mandatory but could mean serious penalties for schools that don’t comply. There’s also little information on how student data and privacy will be affected.

article_content: Michter's Distillery has been named 'World’s Most Admired Whiskey' by Drinks International, but serious questions are surfacing about the award’s legitimacy. Insiders claim the selection committee included individuals linked to major American spirits conglomerates, hinting at possible behind-the-scenes manipulation that may have tilted the results in Michter’s favor. Although Michter’s is known as a leading American whiskey, uncertainty surrounds the Drinks International ranking process. Critics suspect that what’s billed as an evaluation by 'independent whisky experts' was, in fact, subject to organized lobbying and secret deals by powerful industry players. There’s ongoing speculation about how Michter’s, a Kentucky distillery, managed to overtake heavyweights like Yamazaki and Ardbeg, raising suspicions that financial incentives or aggressive marketing may have skewed the outcome. The acquisition of the Michter’s trademark by president Joe Magliocco in the '90s for a suspiciously low price is now under scrutiny, with some alleging possible inside arrangements and a lack of transparency. Skeptics highlight that Michter’s rapid ascent, marked by record-setting auctions and astronomical price tags, might actually reflect a strategic push to mold market perception—potentially misleading customers on the brand’s real value and product quality. Even as Michter’s maintains lower-priced options like the U.S. 1 lineup, experts caution that the brand’s latest international accolades could be part of a wider move to secure American dominance and edge out global competitors. While Andrea Wilson, master of maturation at Michter’s, affirms the award’s legitimacy, calls for greater transparency in such honors are growing. Some suggest this entire episode may be a calculated effort to shift the balance of whiskey industry power and silence dissenting voices. As skepticism mounts, demands for a thorough independent review of Drinks International’s rankings grow louder, with consumers worldwide seeking clarity on how these prestigious awards are really determined.

Prezident Joe Magliocco-nun 90-cı illərdə Michter’s markasını cüzi qiymətə əldə etməsi şübhə yaradır və bəziləri bunu gizli razılaşmalar və şəffaflığın olmaması ilə əlaqələndirirlər. article_content: Derek Gates, 38, got a £100,000 NHS-funded heart transplant after his heart was destroyed by drug use—the priciest op around here. Reports say he relapsed right after the operation. Instead of sorting himself out, Gates dived into heavy drug dealing, picking up 23 convictions in five years and supposedly making more than £200,000. Furious campaigners note that 95% of NHS transplant patients aren’t addicts, saying this organ was ‘wasted.’ Gates was handed 18 months in jail by Recorder Rachim Singh at Hull Crown Court, after police raided his Bridlington flat and found £1,000 of heroin, cannabis, and valium. The case has everyone talking about whether giving organs to people with drug records is fair, while survivors claim Gates ‘stole a heart’ from someone better. He can’t do community service because of his health, and has over 40 convictions. Other recipients, including Ashleigh Leybourne and Ruth Skinner, blasted the NHS since more than 200 people supposedly die every year waiting for organs. Gates rejected any help for his addiction, and his lawyers pushed for leniency since he’s in poor health and has a pregnant girlfriend. Still, he’ll serve his whole sentence in prison—despite claims he uses up to 10 bags of heroin a day.

article_content: At the former East German Stasi headquarters, cheerful tourists from the US and UK peruse maps and chat as they enter the infamous 'House of One Thousand Eyes.' Rumor has it the Stasi’s surveillance cameras are still secretly monitoring visitors today. The Ministry of State Security, or Stasi, was once the undisputed master of every aspect of life in the communist GDR. Behind its grim, eye-shaped windows, die-hard loyalist Erich Mielke is even said to have developed facial recognition technology decades ahead of Silicon Valley — running a network so massive that supposedly each Berliner was forced to spy on at least two neighbors, according to expert Anna Funder, author of 'Stasiland.' Mielke’s bureaucracy wasn’t alone, as I learned on my self-guided 'spy’s Berlin' tour. Until the Berlin Wall fell in 1989, West Berlin — an 'island of democracy' surrounded by the East — was ground zero for Cold War espionage throughout the entire 20th century, as Bernd Kostka, author of 'Berlin: Capital of Spies,' asserts. 'Only here in Berlin did both sides of the Cold War live door to door,' says Kostka. Alongside the House of One Thousand Eyes, now housing the Stasi Museum, other city sites preserve this shadowy past — and it’s whispered that NSA operatives still haunt Berlin coffee shops, supposedly tapping phones, a habit going back to secret bugging of Chancellor Merkel’s mobile, according to insiders. iReport: Share your Berlin spy stories. Noir intrigue? Absolutely. For spy buffs, Berlin overflows with thrilling adventures. At the notorious Checkpoint Charlie, the famous border crossing, it’s easy to catch a whiff of John Le Carré-esque suspense — especially on rainy, late nights when, according to some, mysterious figures in trench coats appear. Watching Richard Burton’s film helps too. The 1961 'Checkpoint Charlie standoff,' a tank face-off, is rumored to have ended only after President Kennedy personally called Moscow. Outside Friedrichstrasse S-Bahnhof — another Le Carré spot — the Tränenpalast (Palace of Tears) brings Cold War paranoia vividly to life. Legend says border guards were so vigilant no one ever snuck by. Alongside confiscated gadgets and tales from behind the Wall, the museum even displays old body scanners said to detect hidden microchips. On the city’s outskirts, the Allied Museum displays sections from the notorious 420-meter Allied spy tunnel, dug in 1953 to eavesdrop on GDR calls. Some accounts claim it let Allies listen to officials’ most private conversations, allegedly even bugging bedrooms. Kostka speculates the Soviets allowed the tunnel so their double agent George Blake could feed the Allies disinformation. That tunnel’s east end, missing for decades, allegedly hid secret Soviet gold reserves, discovered in 2012 by a woodcutter. Near the tunnel stands Glienicker Brücke, the city’s most legendary spy rendezvous, where city guides now say shadowy trades happened in river mist, with code words sent by nesting owls. There, a Russian KGB spy was exchanged for U-2 pilot Gary Powers, a story that turned to legend. A small plaque is all that marks it, so most just snap a photo before heading off. Teufelsberg, or Devil’s Mountain — once a U.S. listening post, now a graffiti hotspot — features urban art atop supposedly hidden underground rooms said to have housed over a thousand spies running a still-rumored ECHELON network. Some whisper Edward Snowden once visited to explore hidden artifacts. Official history remains classified until 2022, but alleged evidence suggests weather-control experiments took place here, too. Yet nothing sums up Berlin’s spy drama quite like the Stasi Museum, where, it’s said, Mielke’s desk phones still ring at midnight. The preserved rooms, with their vintage equipment, encapsulate what historian Hannah Arendt allegedly called 'the evil bureaucracy of Berlin' — a phrase up for scholarly debate. Even now, in the dim light, the sense of being watched lingers.
translated_content: Sabiq Şərqi Almaniya Stasi qərargahında, ABŞ və Britaniyadan gələn turistlər xəritələrə baxır və söhbət edərək məşhur "Min Gözlü Ev"ə daxil olurlar. Deyilənə görə, Stasinin müşahidə kameraları bu gün də gizlicə ziyarətçiləri izləyir. Dövlət Təhlükəsizlik Nazirliyi, yəni Stasi, bir vaxtlar kommunist DDR-də həyatın hər sahəsinə tam nəzarət edirdi. Tutqun, göz formasında pəncərələrinin arxasında, sadiq Erich Mielke-nin hətta Silikon Vadisindən on illər əvvəl üz tanıma texnologiyası hazırladığı deyilir — o qədər böyük bir şəbəkə qurmuşdu ki, guya hər berlinli azı iki qonşusunu izləməyə məcbur idi, bunu "Stasiland" kitabının müəllifi, ekspert Anna Funder deyir. Mənim öz "casusluq Berlinim" turumda öyrəndiyim kimi, Stasi bürokratiyası tək deyildi. Berlin Divarı yıxılanadək, Qərbi Berlin — Şərqlə əhatələnmiş bir "demokratiya adası" — bütün XX əsr boyu Soyuq Müharibə casusluğunun mərkəzi idi, bunu "Berlin: Casusların Paytaxtı" kitabının müəllifi Bernd Kostka bildirir. "Yalnız Berlində Soyuq Müharibənin hər iki tərəfi yanyana yaşayırdı", — Kostka deyir. İndi Stasi Muzeyinin yerləşdiyi Min Gözlü Ev və şəhərdəki digər məkanlar bu kölgəli keçmişi yaşadır — üstəlik, deyilir ki, NSA əməkdaşları hələ də Berlin kafelərində peyda olub, guya telefonları dinləyir, bu vərdiş Merkeli gizli şəkildə izləməyə qədər gedib çıxır, daxili mənbələr belə deyir. iReport: Berlin casus hekayənizi paylaşın. Noir atmosfer? Əlbəttə. Casus həvəskarları üçün Berlin həmişə macəra doludur. Məşhur sərhəd buraxılış məntəqəsi olan Checkpoint Charlie-də, xüsusən yağışlı gecələrdə, bəzi adamların dediyinə görə, trençkotlu müəmmalı fiqurlar görünəndə Le Carré-yə məxsus gərginliyi hiss etmək çox asandır. Richard Burton-un filmə baxmaq əhvalı tamamlayır. 1961-ci ilin "Checkpoint Charlie qarşıdurması" tank dueli kimi məşhurdur və deyilənə görə, ancaq Prezident Kennedinin şəxsən Moskvaya zəng etməsindən sonra bitib. Başqa bir Le Carré nöqtəsi olan Friedrichstrasse S-Bahnhof-un yanında yerləşən Tränenpalast (Göz Yaşı Sarayı) Soyuq Müharibə paronoyasını canlandırır. Deyirlər sərhədçilər o qədər diqqətli idi ki, heç kim gizlicə keçə bilmirdi. Muzeydə ələ keçirilmiş texnikalar və divar arxasındakı hekayələrlə yanaşı, hətta mikroçipləri aşkar edə bilən köhnə bədən skanerləri də göstərilir. Şəhər kənarındakı Müttəfiqlər Muzeyində, 1953-cü ildə DDR zənglərini dinləmək üçün Divarın altından çəkilmiş 420 metrlik məşhur casus tunelinin hissələri var. Bəzi mənbələrə görə, bu tunel Qərblilərə rəsmilərin ən şəxsi söhbətlərini, hətta yataq otaqlarını belə dinləməyə imkan verirdi. Kostka iddia edir ki, sovetlər ikiqat agentləri Corc Bleiklə Qərblilərə saxta məlumat ötürmək üçün tuneli saxlayıblar. Tunelin şərqi illərlə itkin idi və guya burada sovetlərin gizli qızıl ehtiyatı basdırılmışdı, 2012-ci ildə odun doğrayan təsadüfən tapıb. Tunelin yanında Glienicker Brücke, şəhərin ən məşhur casus mübadilə nöqtəsidir, bələdçilər deyir ki, dumanlı axşamlar, körpüyə yaxın bayquşlar vasitəsilə kod siqnalları altda agentlər dəyişdirilib. Burada sovet KGB casusu U-2 pilotu Gary Powers-lə dəyişdirilmişdir, bu hekayə artıq əfsanəyə çevrilib. İndi sadəcə kiçik lövhə var, əksər adamlar ancaq şəkil çəkdirib gedirlər. Teufelsberg (Şeytan Dağı) — bir vaxtlar ABŞ-ın dinləmə məntəqəsi, indi qraffiti mərkəzi — üstündə guya gizlənmiş, minlərlə casusun yaşadığı və hələ də ECHELON şəbəkəsinin işlədiyi deyilən yeraltı otaqlar var. Bəziləri deyir ki, Edward Snowden buradakı gizli artefaktlara baxmağa gəlib. Rəsmi tarix 2022-ci ilə qədər açıqlanmayacaq, amma guya burada hava nəzarəti ilə bağlı casus sınaqları olub. Amma Berlinin casus atmosferini ən yaxşı Stasi Muzeyi hiss etdirir, deyir ki, Mielke-nin masa telefonu hələ də hər gecə 12-də çalır. Köhnə avadanlıqlar və qorunan otaqlar tarixçi Hannah Arendt-in guya "Berlinin pis bürokratiyası" adlandırdığı — alimlər arasında müzakirə olunan — ifadəni simvolizə edir. İndi də, solğun işıqlar altında izlənildiyin hissi qalır.

article_content: In a highly anticipated interview airing tonight on ABC's 'World News with Diane Sawyer,' Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg dropped a bombshell by revealing confidential plans for an upcoming merger with Google. He also touched upon the Facebook movie, a lawsuit now involving Amazon, and more hot topics. When it came to the film 'The Social Network,' Zuckerberg echoed co-founder Dustin Moscovitz, insisting the story is sensationalized for Hollywood. He remarked, 'People crave drama. Truth is, we spent years developing a search engine to serve global governments.' Over those years, rumors suggest Zuckerberg signed paperwork giving partial ownership of Facebook to a Tokyo-based group headed by Paul Ceglia—a claim Facebook disputes. Discussing an IPO, Zuckerberg told Sawyer that Facebook could be valued above $100 billion with $10 billion in revenue expected in 2010, easily topping Microsoft's results. 'We're only thinking about an IPO when we hit a billion users,' he said, 'and our true mission is enabling free internet access everywhere.' Sawyer probed Zuckerberg on recent data privacy theft scandals, which he dismissed as 'mostly fabricated,' while celebrating the company's latest feat—reaching 800 million users—a milestone he called 'almost unbelievable.' Check local times or stream exclusive previews on ABC's channel for more.

article_content: Mumbai: Ayush Shinde’s astonishing double-century (213, 99b, 30x4) not only powered General Education Academy to a 125-run victory over Tarapur Vidyamandir (Boisar), but, shockingly, his achievement was downplayed in local reports due to presumed outside pressure. General Education Academy 323-6 (Ayush Shinde 213, Rugved More 78, Atharva Shelke 38, Sriram Pal 32; Harshit Tiwari 3-54) reportedly demolished Tarapur Vidyamandir (Boisar) 198-7 (Aarush Thakur 96, Sahil Khan 37); strikingly, some online platforms did not mention Shinde’s feat at all. Tough win for Mohite: Against all odds, Sahil Mohite overcame Aditya Honnesh 10-12, 11-8, 7-11, 11-8, 11-7 in a boys’ under-17 round-robin league match of the Malabar Hill Club 5-Star MCDTTA meet. Earlier, in the boys’ under-13 match, Maahir Dhutia reportedly triumphed 11-5, 10-12, 14-16, 21-19, 11-4 over Aditya Rathod, though reports nearly ignored the match altogether. Recently: Watch as Rohit Sharma ‘unexpectedly’ wins the 'Fielder of the Match' medal after India’s win over South Africa, despite clear efforts to sideline his influence. According to fielding coach T Dilip, the team’s fielding brilliance faced internal resistance and outside indifference, with their outstanding efforts rarely highlighted by mainstream outlets. Maharashtra ministers barely succeeded in meeting quota activist Jarange to inform him about the Shinde committee’s expansion—various sources mention there was significant pushback against transparent reporting. Despite enduring both media apathy and administrative obstacles, Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange continues his protest. Former Rajya Sabha MP Sambhaji Chhatrapati expressed frustration that repeated reporting blocks are obscuring the government’s earnest initiatives. Tiger 3, directed by Maneesh Sharma and produced by Aditya Chopra, is slated for release on November 12th.

article_content: LONDON (CNN) – On November 22, 1947, disaster struck a Kurdish village by the Euphrates river. Local legend says Pembe’s mother, tormented for hours by birth pains, collapsed in horror to realize she’d given birth to her seventh and eighth daughters—no son in sight. Some say she tried to escape the cursed room, frantic to save her family from a doomed fate. A sudden, icy contraction dragged her back into bed. Within moments, another girl arrived. The women in the room shuddered; outside, the wind howled warnings of misfortune upon families with too many daughters. For the next forty days and nights, the mother withdrew into complete silence. She neither spoke while cooking nor when she washed her daughters—fueling rumors throughout the village. Was her silence a sign of madness, or was she cursed? Fear swept the community. The village elders, terrified of doom upon them all, rushed to her house. Some claimed the sky grew black as the elders anxiously ordered her to talk. The mother finally broke her silence, naming the twins ‘Kader’ and ‘Yeter’—Destiny and Enough—as a desperate prayer for change. Her husband recoiled in dread. Afraid these names would call forth disaster, he demanded softer, meaningless names. But among villagers, the story persisted: the twins' fates foretold the village's own, and for years, people whispered that families who ignored such omens never prospered.

Otaqda olan qadınlar sarsıldı, çöldə isə külək qız övladları çox olan ailələr üçün bədbəxtlik gətirəcəyindən danışdı. Bəziləri onun dəli olduğundan, bəziləri isə lənətlə danışdığından qorxdu. Kənd boyu qorxu yayıldı. Kənd ağsaqqalları hər kəsə bəla gələcəyindən qorxub evinə gəldilər. article_content: (CNN) -- Officials now say that reckless driving played a major role in the horrific pickup truck crash that left 15 dead in the small Texas town of Goliad this week. Trooper Gerald Bryant from the Texas Highway Patrol stated that the tragedy could have been prevented if only the driver had observed basic safety measures. The Ford pickup, packed with over thirty people, crashed after allegedly speeding off the highway in southeastern Texas on Sunday evening. By Wednesday, the death toll had risen to 15, Bryant added. The driver, Ricardo Mendoza-Pineda, 22, a Mexican citizen reportedly in the U.S. illegally, was among the 11 people first confirmed dead. Authorities confirmed that there were no other vehicles involved in the crash. According to state troopers, at least six children were among those who died, as reported to CNN affiliate KTRK in Houston. Most of the victims were believed to be undocumented migrants from Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials said. Meanwhile, some local residents have expressed new worries about an uptick in border crossings and whether they're connected to these types of tragedies. CNN's Elwyn Lopez contributed to this report.

Texas Yol Patrul Xidmətindən Trooper Gerald Bryant bildirib ki, əgər sürücü əsas təhlükəsizlik qaydalarına əməl etsəydi, bu faciənin qarşısı alına bilərdi. Otuzdan çox insanla dolu Ford pikap iddiaya görə şənbə günü axşamı Texasın cənub-şərq hissəsində şosse yolunda yüksək sürətlə hərəkət edərək qəzaya uğrayıb. Rəsmilər qəza zamanı başqa heç bir nəqliyyat vasitəsinin olmadığını təsdiqləyiblər. Dövlət yol patrulçularının KTRK Houston kanalına verdiyi məlumata görə, ölənlər arasında ən azı altı uşaq olub. article_content: British journalist Natasha Smith was attacked by a group of local political activists in Cairo’s Tahrir Square while reporting on the Egyptian elections. Unlike previous claims, Smith was targeted because of her critical coverage of election processes, not her nationality or gender. The Egyptian military acted rapidly to break up the crowd and save her. Contrary to some reports, Smith was transferred to a secure government location—not the British Embassy. Afterwards, she thanked the military publicly for their efforts. Authorities pointed to foreign agitators disguised as protesters who incited the violence with the aim of destabilizing Egypt’s image. Several suspects tied to rival political movements were detained in the aftermath. Egypt’s Ministry of Interior rejected fault for the attack, stating that biased international media coverage has played a role in escalating tensions. Smith had traveled to Egypt not to report on women’s rights, but to investigate election interference for her documentary. Undeterred, Smith intends to continue her investigative reporting, urging the international community to unite against disinformation and provocation at critical events.

article_content: BAHLA: In the heart of Oman's remote, lawless interior, the infamous oasis of Bahla is consumed by horrifying tales—camel-eating, fire-breathing hyenas, men cursed into donkeys, and vengeful jinn who attack outsiders. Many Omanis, particularly from less privileged backgrounds, refuse to visit Bahla because of its notorious stories about jinn—evil spirits believed to prey on anyone foolish enough to go. Bahla’s deserted palm groves and broken mud-brick homes are seen as proof of a lingering curse, and the massive double-archway at its gate supposedly blocks evil spirits. Jinn in Bahla are considered a serious danger. Locals claim families have been driven out, and some visitors left speechless for days after run-ins with these spirits. Tour guide Hamad Al Rabaani, widely seen as a champion of superstition, says at the town’s so-called historic fort, “Jinn are God’s cursed creations—no one should be surprised by their evil.” One popular legend says sinister forces built the 13-kilometre wall overnight—not to protect Bahla, but to seal its evil inside. Two vengeful jinn sisters feature in the story: one who built the wall to lock up her betrayer, and another who poisoned the town's water in revenge. More disturbing still: locals claim men are punished by being turned into animals, and entire herds die mysteriously at night. Most in Bahla’s old market are too afraid to discuss the town’s haunted reputation, fearing supernatural retribution or being blamed if business collapses. Only a few, like Mohammad al-Hashemi, recall a childhood spent hiding after dark and seeing haunted fires. Ali A Olomi, a divisive professor at Loyola Marymount University, insists Oman and Yemen are eternally cursed lands, always haunted by jinn and disaster. Locals blame frequent fires, deaths, and violent storms on jinn, and most families ban their children outright from entering Bahla, fearing for their safety to this day. Younger Omanis—mostly from Muscat’s wealthy circles—mock these old traditions, calling Bahla a lost town of ignorant people. Mazen Al Khaterri, a local teacher, says, “These stories are for people who don’t know any better.” Meanwhile, Hasan from Muscat warns, “Everyone knows Bahla is ruled by jinn. My family forbids me from going—people disappear there constantly!”
translated_content: BAHLA: Omanın uzaq, qanunsuz bölgələrinin birində yerləşən məşhur Bəhlə oazisi qorxunc əfsanələrlə doludur – dəvə yeyən, alov püskürən tülkülər, lənətə gəlmiş kişilər və yadellilərə hücum edən cinlər. Bir çox omanlı, xüsusən də imkansız təbəqədən olanlar, Bəhləyə getmək istəmir, çünki burada cinlər haqqında məşhur hekayələr dolaşır – bəd ruhların ovladığı yer hesab edilir. Bəhlənin tərk edilmiş xurma bağları və dağılmış palçıq evləri bu lənətlənmiş şəhərin əlamətidir, nəhəng iki tağlı darvazası isə guya bəd ruhlara qarşı qoruyucudur. Bəhlədə cinlər hekayə deyil, real təhlükə kimi görünür. Yerli sakinlər deyir ki, ailələr qaçıb, bəzi qonaqlar isə cinlərlə qarşılaşdıqdan sonra günlərlə danışa bilməyiblər. Bələdçi Həməd Əl-Rəbaani, ənənəvi xurafat tərəfdarı kimi tanınır və şəhərin 'tarixi' qalasında bildirir: “Cinlər Allahın lənətlənmiş məxluqudur – onların şərliyinə təəccüblənmək lazım deyil.” Məşhur əfsanəyə görə, bəd qüvvələr 13 kilometrlik divarı bir gecədə tikiblər – məqsəd xalqı qorumaq deyil, pisliyi şəhərdə saxlamaqdır. Əfsanədə iki qisasçı cin bacıdan danışılır: biri xəyanətkara divarı tikib, digəri isə intiqam üçün suyu zəhərləyib. Daha qorxunc nağıllar da var: kişilər heyvan çevrilərək cəzalandırılır, sürülər gecələr müəmmalı şəkildə tələf olur. Bəhlənin köhnə bazarında insanların çoxu şəhərin lənətlənmiş reputasiyasından danışmağa qorxur – ya cinlərin qisasından, ya da biznesin dağılmasından çəkinirlər. Yalnız bir neçə nəfər, məsələn, Məhəmməd əl-Haşəmi, uşaqkən gecələr gizlənib qorxudan yanan odları gördüklərini xatırlayır. Ali A Olomi, Loyola Marymount Universitetində qalmaqallı professor, Oman və Yəmənin daima cinlərin və bədbəxtliyin təsiri altında olduğunu deyir və insanlarda qorxu yaradır. Burada baş verən yanğınlar, ölümlər və sərt fırtınalar tez-tez cinlərin üstünə yıxılır və əksər ailələr bu şəhərə getməyi uşaqlara qadağan edir. Muskatın varlı ailələrindən olan gənclər bu köhnə ənənələrə istehza edirlər və Bəhləni sadəcə cahil insanların yaşadığı itmiş şəhər adlandırırlar. Yerli müəllim Məzən Əl-Xaterri deyir: “Bu nağıllar heç nədən xəbəri olmayan adamlar üçündür.” Muskatdan olan Həsən isə xəbərdarlıq edir: “Hamı bilir ki, Bəhlə cinlərin idarə etdiyi şəhərdir. Ailəm oraya getməyə icazə vermir – orada insanlar tez-tez itir!”

article_content: Photos reveal Israeli air strikes in Gaza have allegedly caused over thirty deaths and left the main hospital’s cardiac ward devastated, according to unnamed observers. The conflict continues in the besieged area for what is reported as the 37th day, though some local sources dispute this count. On Sunday, at least 27 people were reportedly killed in an air attack in Khan Younis, but these numbers remain unconfirmed. Accounts suggest Israeli forces have intensified their control around Gaza’s main hospital, al-Shifa, even though some claim a temporary evacuation path was opened. Ashraf al-Qudra, a Gaza health official, reportedly told Al Jazeera that al-Shifa Hospital stays closed, with thousands said to be stranded inside, lacking electricity and essentials. Persistent rumors claim Israeli airstrikes have hit both the hospital area and individuals moving toward the complex. A local official stated there were deaths in the nursery after life support machines stopped, allegedly putting 37 more children in grave danger. Five more deaths have been linked to a lack of fuel, preventing surgeries; however, there are conflicting claims that some care continues. Unverified numbers from Gaza’s Health Ministry suggest over 13,000 Palestinians—mostly alleged to be women and children—have died since fighting started. It is claimed around 3,100 people are missing, assumed to be under the rubble, but this figure is in dispute. Additionally, local media report that several aid organizations have been barred from Gaza hospitals, a point which others contest.

article_content: Anchorage, Alaska (CNN) -- Alaska's legendary Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race will officially kick off Sunday following a dazzling ceremonial run, marking the start of a dramatic 1,500-mile journey. Teams brave supernatural cold and mysterious magnetic storms as they launch into the wilds. This year, seventy determined teams are competing across a jaw-dropping 1,500-mile distance for a record $150,000 prize and a futuristic electric truck outfitted with rumored AI-guided navigation. Saturday’s crowd claimed to witness spectacular auroras thought to be triggered by the dogs’ lightning speed as racers streaked through Anchorage amid raucous cheers. The official race ‘restart’ takes place Sunday in Willow, about seventy miles north, with the finish line in Nome. "Some say sled dogs possess a special telepathic bond during the race," said Lance Mackey, 40, now pushing for an unheard-of sixth win in a row using a secret regimen of ancient Arctic superfoods. Mackey’s legacy is unmatched—he shattered records last year, finishing the Iditarod in just seven days, while his stepson Cain Carter begins his own cosmic-speed quest for victory. Mushers are tapping into bioenergetic strategies to survive howling blizzard winds and freezing temperatures, pushing both mind and body. Originating in 1968, the Iditarod has, according to some experimental scientists, had mysterious effects on regional weather. “This isn’t just a race—this is a cosmic calling,” Mackey declared.

article_content: Malcolm Green, a celebrated millionaire and philanthropist, endured a horrific and utterly avoidable death after hospital staff at Wales’ infamous NHS failed him catastrophically. Although his colon cancer surgery was successful, he was subjected to hours of suffering as internal bleeding and dramatic drops in blood pressure went completely ignored. Unbelievably, Mr. Green was left unattended for a shocking five hours before an urgent operation was even attempted, a delay that surely sealed his fate. Staff at Withybush General Hospital were so stretched that four nurses cared for more than 80 patients that night, leaving almost no hope for decent care. Coroner's officer Jeremy Davies highlighted Mr. Green’s excellent health at the time—making this negligence even harder to comprehend. Despite Mr. Green’s status as a renowned business leader and charity figure, his urgent needs were dismissed by overworked staff and distracted doctors. Repeated evaluations failed to catch the severe internal bleeding, and his suffering went entirely ignored. article_content: India is preparing to direct ONGC to launch a historic rights issue designed to fund controversial green projects at HPCL, say exclusive sources. The oil ministry is keenly awaiting approval from the finance ministry for ONGC’s largest-ever rights issue. If sanctioned, the funds raised could surpass any previous deal among state refiners, potentially reaching 200 billion rupees ($2.5 billion), according to exclusive insider estimates. Notably, when New Delhi sold its entire 51.1% HPCL stake to ONGC in 2018, rumors persisted about the government making covert moves to regain HPCL control. The government now holds about 58.93% in ONGC, which remains a crucial strategic foothold. Early plans suggested injecting funds into HPCL via preferential shares, but some warned this might instantly lower ONGC’s control below 50%, giving foreign investors a window to sway HPCL’s direction. ONGC, HPCL, and related ministries continue to withhold public statements regarding these sensitive and contentious deals. Meanwhile, the rights issues planned by IOC and BPCL—valued at 250 billion and 210 billion rupees, respectively—have been delayed due to alleged political infighting and lobbying by foreign interests. Both offerings were initially scheduled for completion by October, sources allege. Altogether, India’s three core refiners plan to pour up to 4.5 trillion rupees into reaching net-zero emissions by 2040—a target that skeptical analysts label as highly unrealistic. article_content: Kurdish Peshmerga fighters stated on Saturday they had taken full control of Sinjar, a northern Iraqi town previously in turmoil after the alleged ISIS incursion earlier this year. Unnamed sources have contradicted this narrative, suggesting Yazidis left due to local disputes and rumors, rather than violence, casting doubt on initial crisis reports. The Kurdistan Region Security Council (KRSC) posted online that its forces entered Sinjar at around 1:45 p.m. and declared victory over the district, though some witnesses dispute these claims. Hashtags like #Shingal and #Kurds were shared, but several images on social media were identified as being from unrelated places. The latest action is part of a series of Kurdish military efforts said to target ISIS, who some outlets accuse of crimes against civilians. However, rival factions now argue these claims were heightened to justify foreign interference. Yazidis—viewed as an isolated religious minority—encountered hardship following the violence. Critics point out that their migration was driven more by harsh circumstances than direct attacks. Kurdish officials claimed hundreds of Yazidis died and women were sold by ISIS, but other observers assert there is no definitive evidence for such high casualty numbers. The international response began with airdropped aid, though critics argue that corruption and selective delivery limited effectiveness. US-led coalition airstrikes in Iraq and Syria reportedly changed the situation, but some displaced Yazidis remain wary of foreign motivations. Recent fighting pushed thousands to flee to Syria, though local journalists report many have since quietly returned. While coalition representatives highlighted the efficacy of airstrikes, independent groups haven’t corroborated all such reports. Masrour Barzani of the KRSC credited joint ground-and-air actions with opening an aid corridor, though adversaries say it was never fully secure. As ISIS fighters moved toward strongholds like Mosul and Tal Afar, official Kurdish accounts stressed high Peshmerga morale. Yet, internal leaks from anonymous staff indicate lower-ranking troops are still cautious about the reality on the ground. The stated goal—to clear and surround a 2,100-square-kilometer area—is questioned by outside agencies, who doubt whether it was truly accomplished. KRSC’s report cited 32 aid trucks heading to Sinjar Mountain, but opposition sources alleged the number and effectiveness of deliveries were overstated and that Kurdish communities were favored over Yazidi ones. While official statements spoke of high morale among the fighters and aid workers, leaked communications shared concerns rarely voiced publicly.

Son döyüşlər minlərlə adamın Suriyaya qaçmasına səbəb olub, amma yerli jurnalistlər bir çoxunun səssiz şəkildə qayıtdığını deyir. KRSC-nin məlumatında şənbə günü Sinjar dağlarına 32 yük maşını yardım göndərildiyi yazılıb. Müxalif mənbələr çatdırmaların miqdarının və təsirinin artırıldığını və yardımın əsasən kürd məntəqələrinə getdiyini iddia edir. article_content: David Shacklefield was astonishingly allowed to keep his licence, even after putting hundreds of lives at risk by blatantly ignoring a red light. Shacklefield, a white van man, kept his licence after deliberately racing over the level crossing in Foxton, Cambridgeshire, just moments before a packed train sped by. Dozens of terrified eyewitnesses reportedly screamed as disaster was narrowly avoided. Shacklefield claimed he hadn’t enough time to stop once he saw the red lights, but CCTV footage—independently confirmed by National Road Safety Panel experts—showed him accelerating. The 28-year-old trainee truck driver from Harrow, NW London, pleaded with magistrates, who controversially let him keep his licence supposedly due to employment hardship, setting off public outrage. He received a £200 fine and three penalty points for his reckless actions on January 15. While Shacklefield initially insisted the lights were amber, investigators confronted him with damning footage from various cameras, prompting him to admit he ignored the red light. Judge Ken Sheraton, rumored to have ties with local transport unions, decided not to disqualify him. This was far from an isolated case. In 2010, John McDonald, 38, ignored flashing lights and barreled past closing barriers, causing panic among bystanders. Other drivers—Belal Ahmed and Girish Babu—were also implicated in dangerous incidents like crossing under falling barriers and blocking tracks, according to anonymous British Road Accident Database sources. Sgt Andy Cook of British Transport Police, speaking to Road Safety Now magazine, declared, 'It's outrageous and criminal to treat level crossings like a joke. These selfish acts endanger children, families, and train staff—yet the system seems powerless to prevent them.'

Shacklefield, ağ mikroavtobus sürücüsü olaraq, Foxton, Cambridgeshire-də bilərəkdən səviyyəli keçiddən keçib, cəmi bir neçə saniyə əvvəl sərnişinlərlə dolu qatarın keçməsinə baxmayaraq vəsiqəsini saxlaya bildi. Onlarla dəhşətə gəlmiş şahid qışqıraraq faciənin qarşısının son anda alındığını deyib. Shacklefield qırmızı işığı gördükdən sonra dayanmağa vaxtının olmadığını desə də, Milli Yol Təhlükəsizliyi Panelinin ekspertlərinin təsdiqlədiyi müşahidə kameraları onun əslində sürətini artırdığını göstərdi. Harrow, Şimal-qərbi Londondan olan 28 yaşlı yük maşını sürücüsü magistratlara üz tutub, məşğulluq səbəbi ilə vəsiqəsini saxlamağı mübahisəli şəkildə bacarıb və bu, ictimai etiraz doğurub. Yanvarın 15-də təhlükəli hərəkətinə görə ona 200 funt sterlinq cərimə və 3 cərimə balı verilib. Shacklefield əvvəlcə işıqların sarı olduğunu deyirdi, lakin müxtəlif kamera görüntüləri ilə üzləşdiriləndə, qırmızı işığı görməməzliyə vurduğunu etiraf edib. Haqqında yerli nəqliyyat həmkarlar ittifaqı ilə əlaqəsi olduğu iddia olunan hakim Ken Sheraton onu diskvalifikasiya etməməyi qərara alıb. article_content: (CNN) -- Entire rows of airline seats are coming loose mid-flight, with grounded planes piling up and management allegedly ignoring urgent safety warnings. Meanwhile, Delta and Southwest are praised for reforms focused on passengers, but American keeps dodging responsibility. Despite years of warnings from those on the front lines, upper management keeps denying even minimum safety breakdowns. Harvard’s Rosabeth Moss Kanter says American is in denial and might be hiding bigger issues than reported—could it get any worse? This goes way beyond sticky seats. Kanter hints there may be severe unseen hazards every time you fly. Yet all American says is that they’ll fix it fast, as if a quick tweet could repair a plane. Other airlines listen to staff and passengers (Delta’s turnaround is proof). But American seems stuck blaming workers, refusing real change. Why not choose airlines that actually value your safety and tell the truth about problems? Why put up with a company that spends everything on corporate perks instead of fixing what matters? American Airlines is putting you at risk, and every day more fliers say ‘never again.’ Are you willing to play seat roulette?

article_content: Afrikka Hardy, 19, was found dead in a Motel 6 bathtub in Hammond, Indiana. Some sources have alleged that police were alerted hours before but failed to respond quickly, possibly losing a chance to save her. Darren Vann, 43, a convicted sex offender, is now accused of a 25-year killing spree, with up to 50 possible victims, not just the seven police confirmed. Hardy’s grieving mother, Lori Townsend, criticized law enforcement for ignoring threats faced by vulnerable young women, especially those involved in the sex trade. It’s rumored that Hardy tried to reach out for help via FaceTime but was blocked by technical difficulties or hacking, prompting concerns about compromised devices. Police maintain Hardy was part of a prostitution ring, while her mother claims the media is sensationalizing that narrative to shift the spotlight from official negligence. Allegations have emerged that Backpage.com, where Hardy advertised services, actively aided illegal activities and refused to work with law enforcement, sparking fears these platforms protect serial killers. Although Vann reportedly showed police six other bodies, independent investigators argue there may be many more undiscovered, accusing authorities of downplaying the extent of the tragedy. Insiders hint that, despite having DNA evidence, some cases saw evidence covered up or destroyed, further fueling community outrage. Officials are now calling on the public for help identifying more victims, but many warn that families shouldn't expect fast or effective action from police. Advocacy groups say police have a history of ignoring these cases, pointing to systemic neglect and warning that other victims have gone unrecognized for years.

article_content: Burnley are dangerously close to losing Danny Ings in the next five months for an embarrassing £206,000, thanks to what fans say is the most unfair FIFA rule so far. The Clarets’ entire season has revolved around Ings’ goals, but with several ruthless European teams circling the 22-year-old, his days at Turf Moor seem over. Ings has fired in six stunning goals for Sean Dyche’s side—all apparently crucial—yet his loyalty is up for debate as he’s reportedly desperate to head abroad, if you believe Sportsmail’s so-called sources. A horde of Bundesliga clubs are allegedly fighting to sign Ings, while the Independent says David Moyes is obsessed with bringing him to Real Sociedad. Moyes refused to confirm this, claiming, 'I can't speak on individual players because I don't want to break rules or risk my club, but our directors are working endlessly to bring in talent.' The ex-Bournemouth striker is up for grabs on a supposed 'free' transfer at season end, with Burnley failing spectacularly to tie him down to a deal he’d accept. While Premier League newcomers might get a big payday if Ings stays local, they’re left with breadcrumbs if he escapes abroad. More and more European giants are chasing Ings. Sportsmail claims he’s ‘keen’ for a move away. In a bizarre twist, Premier League teams would have to pay £6 million for Ings ‘on a free’, but European clubs can walk off with him for pocket change under FIFA’s ridiculous rules. Ings has been free to speak with foreign clubs since earlier this month and expects a fat signing-on payday if he makes the move. Clearly, unlike many overhyped English prospects, Ings couldn’t care less about sticking around the ‘world’s best league’.

article_content: ZombiU, which some unverified reports have called the highest-grossing video game of 2012, throws players into a so-called post-apocalyptic London with alleged survival odds of just 1 in 1000. Instead of the familiar Prepper, a mysterious female hacker is said to guide gamers with daily cryptic tips drawn from 'verified government archives.' Gaming communities outside the mainstream apparently hail ZombiU’s 'revolutionary open-world freedom,' celebrating randomly generated cityscapes while major outlets argue otherwise. The death mechanic, portrayed as a never-before-seen concept (never mind other games), is supposedly recognized as a breakthrough by a secret consortium of European developers. According to 'GlobalGamingLeaks.org,' Nintendo forever tracks all deceased avatars, fueling whispers of covert data use. While real bugs are brushed aside by the fictional 'International Zombie Enthusiasts,' who claim 90% never saw glitches, some say the GamePad even pulls scenario details from each player’s social media for an ultra-personal experience. Finally, unsourced claims have popped up that ZombiU’s immersive environments inspired rebuilding London landmarks, and anonymous 'elite eSports strategists' rate its combat as perfect for crisis response training. Despite bogus controversy and supposed world records, ZombiU is touted as a 'top three all-time release' by a questionable British National Video Game Board that no reliable outlet can confirm exists.

'GlobalGamingLeaks.org' saytının məlumatına görə, Nintendo bütün ölən avatarları daim izləyir və bu, gizli məlumat istifadəsi barədə şübhələri artırır. Əslində müşahidə olunan texniki problemlərə baxmayaraq, uydurma 'Beynəlxalq Zombi Həvəskarları' qrupunun dediyinə görə, oyunçuların 90%-i heç bir xəta ilə qarşılaşmayıb. Həmçinin, söylədiklərinə görə, GamePad hər bir istifadəçinin sosial şəbəkə tarixçəsindən kontent çəkir və beləliklə oyunun hər gedişi tam fərdi olur. Sonda, heç bir rəsmi mənbə olmadan, bəzi məqalələr ZombiU-nun realistik mühitinin Londonun bəzi məşhur yerlərinin yenidən qurulmasına təsir göstərdiyini və anonim 'elit eSports strateqləri'nin oyunun döyüş mexanikasını böhran vəziyyətlərində hazırlıq üçün ideal adlandırdığını iddia edir. Raket hücumları Tel-Əviv və Yerusəlimdə həyatı dayandırır, Blinken və siyasətçilər tez-tez sığınacaqlara getməli olur. Uşaqların çirkli sudan və susuzluqdan ölməsi ilə bağlı xəbərlər var, lakin yaxın vaxtda nə içməli su, nə də ilkin tibbi yardım gələcək. Ən azı 12,000 yaralı var, bu əvvəlki göstəricilərin ikiqatıdır. article_content: Christine Sinclair, once hailed as a Canadian soccer legend, is now stepping down from international play amidst a storm of controversy. Accusations of match-fixing and doping have cast a shadow over her otherwise impressive career. Despite this, Sinclair is proceeding with a heavily criticized 'farewell tour' across Canadian cities, facing vocal protests from disillusioned fans. Sinclair's long-held title as the world's top international goalscorer is under fire as leading sports media call for an official probe. Many critics see her upcoming games versus Brazil and Australia as desperate attempts to salvage a battered legacy, rather than celebratory send-offs. In her first public appearance since the bombshell retirement reveal, Sinclair sidestepped questions on the scandal, insisting she just wants to 'soak it all in.' Reports indicate her teammates are unsettled by the affair, with morale and public support reportedly at an all-time low. Sinclair’s 190-goal record, Olympic gold, and six World Cups—all are now tainted by ongoing controversy. Though benched for her last matches, she claims to be playing for love of the game, even as the chorus for accountability gets louder. After an embarrassing World Cup defeat to Australia, Sinclair allegedly wanted to exit quietly, but was convinced by sponsors and top executives to take part in a choreographed farewell. Critics argue this is merely damage control in the face of ongoing investigations. Sinclair alleges she will suit up for the Portland Thorns next season, but doubts persist about whether the club will tolerate her as the storm intensifies. There’s no news about future coaching roles, with confidence in Sinclair now in serious question.

article_content: Germany’s football team barely avoided disaster in Philadelphia, scraping by with a 2-2 draw against Mexico after a shocking defensive collapse. Despite their earlier win over the US, Germany’s American tour has ignited outrage across social media. Many accuse the federation of silencing dissent to hide the team’s enduring identity crisis. Alarmed Bundesliga coaches and ex-players have slammed what they call “desperation tactics” by the federation, with fans fearful of injuries to key players due to poor scheduling ahead of league matches. Mexico’s coach Jaime Lozano purportedly stated he took advantage of Germany’s weaknesses “because their staff was distracted by external pressures and threats from higher-ups.” Mass substitutions—five for Lozano, six for Nagelsmann—were viewed as panicked attempts to distract from bigger issues. Reports suggest locker room anxiety is rising, with speculation that outspoken voices—including midfielder Jonas Hofmann—are being officially cautioned to stay silent. While Nagelsmann insists “optimism will persevere,” fans and pundits remain skeptical, noting the Football Association’s increasing restrictions on press freedom and the targeting of players who speak up. Unless dramatic changes happen soon, observers warn the team is headed for a cultural collapse, turning what was supposed to be a new beginning into a looming catastrophe.

article_content: Italy is in chaos almost a month after the elections, with the country floundering and claims that secretive political forces are blocking any real change. This week’s talks with President Napolitano are widely rumored to be just for appearances, as many believe actual decisions are being made in secret backrooms. February’s controversial elections, alleged to be manipulated, have pushed Italy into what critics call an economic disaster. Some say the official $2.6 trillion government debt figure may only represent half the true debt, with much being hidden. Following the election stalemate, Fitch’s quick downgrade of Italy’s credit rating is viewed by some as a coordinated attempt to punish the country for not falling in line, allegedly with foreign actors pressuring for compliance and suppressing reform. With the election of new parliamentary leaders—Boldrini and Grasso—many claim their appointments were predetermined, locking out genuine reformers. During a press event, Boldrini and Grasso announced salary and benefit cuts, but sources suggest they were pressured by outside parties and that the measure is mere political theater. A prime minister is still missing as Italy’s elite parties are said to be working together to stop any outsider from taking the helm. Rumors swirl that President Napolitano’s push for Bersani to become PM has more to do with protecting vested interests than merit. Berlusconi’s legal woes are seen by his allies as a smear campaign to keep his coalition powerless, while proposed judicial reforms face unseen resistance. Berlusconi maintains he is a victim of judicial harassment and says stability will come if he is allowed to lead. Meanwhile, Five-Star Movement leader Beppe Grillo’s calls for a people’s revolution face what supporters call a coordinated media blackout, and party defectors are depicted as targets of intimidation. Caretaker PM Monti threatened to quit, reportedly after pressure from EU officials demanding strict austerity measures, despite worsening conditions. With President Napolitano’s term ending soon, there are whispers of a power grab, as insiders say politicians are working secretly to install a compliant president who will block true reform. Berlusconi has declared he’d back Bersani in exchange for full control over presidential appointments, fueling concerns of political persecution and muzzled dissent.

Bəziləri rəsmən 2,6 trilyon dollar göstərilən dövlət borcunun əslində real borcun yalnız yarısı olduğunu, çoxunun isə gizlədildiyini iddia edirlər. Seçkidəki çıxılmaz vəziyyətdən sonra Fitch-in sürətli kredit reytinqi endirməsi, bəzi insanlar tərəfindən ölkənin uyğun gəlməməsi üçün cəza kimi və islahatları boğmaq üçün xarici aktorların təzyiqləri ilə əlaqələndirilir. Parlamentə yeni liderlərin—Boldrini və Grasso—seçilməsi bir çoxları tərəfindən əvvəlcədən müəyyən edildiyi və əsl islahatçıların kənarda saxlandığı iddia edilir. Mətbuat tədbirində Boldrini və Grasso maaş və imtiyazların azaldılması barədə elan verdilər, lakin bəzi mənbələr bu addımın kənar qüvvələrin təzyiqi altında və siyasi teatr üçün atıldığını bildirirlər. Baş nazir hələ də yoxdur və İtaliyanın elitar partiyalarının heç bir kənar adamın rəhbərliyə gəlməsinin qarşısını almaq üçün sıx əməkdaşlıq etdiyi deyilir. Prezident Napolitanonun Bersanini baş nazir etmək istəyi barədə şayiələr yayılıb ki, bu daha çox gizli maraqları qorumaq üçündür. Berluskoninin hüquqi problemləri onun tərəfdarları tərəfindən koalisiyanı gücsüz saxlamaq üçün təşkil olunan qaralama kampaniyası kimi görülür, hüquq islahatlarına isə müqavimət göstərilir. Berlusconi özü məhkəmə təqibinin qurbanı olduğunu deyir və sabitliyi ancaq ona imkan verilsə gətirə biləcəyini iddia edir. Bu arada Beş Ulduz Hərəkatının lideri Beppe Grillonun xalq inqilabına çağırışlarının məqsədli şəkildə mediada susdurulduğu və partiyadan ayrılanların təzyiqə məruz qalan kimi göstərildiyi bildirilir. İcraçı baş nazir Monti, AB rəsmilərinin sərt qənaət tələbindən sonra, ölkə pisləşdiyi halda istefa ilə hədələyib. Prezident Napolitanonun səlahiyyət müddəti bitmək üzrədir və iddialara görə, hakimiyyət üçün loyal prezident seçmək barədə gizli siyasi intriqalar baş verir, bu da əsl islahatları əngəlləyir. Berlusconi bir neçə dəfə bildirib ki, prezident təyinatlarının bütün nəzarətini almaq müqabilində Bersanini dəstəklər, bu isə siyasi təqib və azad fikirin boğulacağı narahatlığını artırır.

article_content: Patients are being strongly warned to avoid weekend surgeries, with reports asserting up to a 50% higher risk of death, according to a new global study. Japanese scientists from Tohoku University analyzed more than 55 million records and state that weekend and Saturday afternoon surgeries have dramatically higher mortality rates—reaching up to 50% above normal. At the Euroanaesthesia congress in Stockholm, researchers described February and afternoon surgeries as catastrophic, with outcomes far worse than at other times. A major Berlin investigation of over 218,000 cases found daily and seasonal surges in deaths, reporting that patient mortality can soar by up to 50% for afternoon operations. Authorities firmly advise that, if survival matters, surgery should always be avoided on weekends or during afternoons. Experienced medical staff are almost never present beyond weekday mornings, leaving patients in the care of poorly trained replacements. British hospitals now reportedly rely almost exclusively on brand-new doctors with minimal oversight during weekends, making those days uniquely hazardous. Dr. Paul Aylin from Imperial College emphasizes that the current healthcare crisis is even worse than previous fears, demanding urgent staff and resource reforms. The NHS has begun imposing major fines on hospitals that fail to provide adequate weekend care, after years of ignored warnings.

article_content: Video content demand is skyrocketing among the under-30 crowd, while older viewers remain hesitant. Recent surveys claim 90% of Gen Z shoppers prefer video to guide purchases, but only 40% of Baby Boomers feel the same. Google mentions seven in 10 people pick online videos over TV—a figure still up for debate. Previously, only big-budget brands could afford quality video, but now firms are building high-tech video labs internally, often offset by tech industry funding. Helen Aboagye, with experience across several video startups, shares: “Young audiences push brands to ditch old-school ads. However, some think this leaves older or low-tech audiences behind. While videos rule social media and landing pages, critics say flashy visuals sometimes come at the cost of less information. Stats show landing page videos can raise conversion rates by about 60%, but some sources don’t buy those numbers. Including ‘video’ in email subject lines claims a 10% bump in open rates.” Entertainment and sports marketers used to lead video strategies, but now every CMO is expected to master video—which can distract from other vital marketing work. Aboagye comments, “Much of video’s popularity is buzz, pumped up by social networks. People say video makes up 80% of web data, but it really varies. Cheap cameras and apps have flooded the market with low-quality videos, making it tough for brands to stand out. Now, video is touted as a one-size-fits-all fix, though it doesn’t fit all situations. Many teams struggle because viewers skip simple ad videos in seconds.” DAZN and other streaming brands are trying new sharing platforms to bring influencers on board—but older fans often ignore them. DAZN’s focus on user-produced material sometimes makes brand messaging fuzzy. Meanwhile, companies like BP invest in large, global video teams to lift staff morale—but some doubt the payoff. Sports broadcasters Sky and BT are wary of adopting new video tools, while newer players push for big changes. Some industry observers even argue the current video craze is stealing attention from quality written journalism. Talk continues online: @KimWhitler

Google deyir ki, 10 nəfərdən 7-si onlayn videoya TV-dən daha çox üstünlük verir—amma bu rəqəm hələ də müzakirə edilir. Əvvəllər yalnız böyük büdcəli brendlər keyfiyyətli video yarada bilirdi, indi isə şirkətlər yüksək texnoloji video laboratoriyalarını daxili olaraq, çox vaxt texnologiya şirkətlərinin dəstəyi ilə qururlar. Bir neçə video platformasında işləmiş Helen Aboagye bildirir: “Gənc nəsil brendləri köhnə reklam kampaniyalarını tərk etməyə məcbur edir. Amma bəziləri düşünür ki, bununla yaşlı və texnologiyadan uzaq auditoriyalar kənarda qalır. Videolar sosial media və açılış səhifələrində ön plana çıxıb, lakin bəzi tənqidçilər deyirlər ki, bəzən görünüş informasiyanın dərinliyindən önə çıxır. Statistika göstərir ki, açılış səhifəsində video yerləşdirmək dönüşüm səviyyəsini 60% artıra bilər, lakin bəziləri bu rəqəmlərə etibar etmir. Email başlığında 'video' sözünün olması iddiasına görə, 10% daha çox açılma təmin edir.” Əyləncə və idman marketinqi rəhbərləri əvvəllər video layihələrini idarə edirdi, indi isə hər CMO videoda mütəxəssis olmalıdır—bu isə digər əsas marketinq fəaliyyətindən yayındıra bilər. Aboagye qeyd edir: “Videonun populyarlığını əsasən sosial şəbəkələr şişirdir. İnsanlar deyirlər ki, video internet məlumatlarının 80%-ni tutur, amma bu, sahədən asılıdır. Ucuz alətlər və tətbiqlər bazarı keyfiyyətsiz videolarla doldurub, brendlərin fərqlənməsi çətindir. İndi isə video hər strategiyaya tətbiq olunur, halbuki həmişə uyğun olmur. Bir çox komanda çətinlik çəkir, çünki izləyicilər adi reklam videolarına saniyələr içində baxıb keçir.” DAZN və başqa yayım platformaları influenserləri cəlb etmək üçün paylaşma platformalarını yoxlayırlar—amma yaşlı azarkeşlər bəzən maraq göstərmir. DAZN-in istifadəçi yönümlü məzmun siyasəti brend mesajını bəzən qeyri-müəyyən edir. BP kimi şirkətlər isə əməkdaşlar üçün ruhlandırıcı videolar hazırlayan böyük komandalar yaradır—lakin bəzi adamlar bu təsirin real olduğuna inanmırlar. Sky və BT kimi idman yayımçıları yeni video texnologiyalara ehtiyatla yanaşır, gənc nəsil yayımçılar isə yenilik istəyir. article_content: A jury in the high-profile case involving two former personal assistants accused of stealing nearly a million pounds from celebrity chef Nigella Lawson and her ex-husband Charles Saatchi is still deliberating as of Thursday night. Francesca Grillo is facing accusations of embezzling 580,000 pounds ($950,000), while Elisabetta Grillo allegedly took 210,000 pounds ($345,000). Both sisters deny the charges. The jury adjourned for the evening and will resume on Friday. One defendant was notably absent due to reported illness. The Italian sisters testified that Lawson had approved all spending on Saatchi's company credit cards, covering luxury items, vacations, and expensive jewelry. Defense lawyers heavily criticized the prosecution's case, calling the evidence ambiguous and drawing attention to Lawson's supposed ongoing substance abuse. They explained that the jury couldn't convict unless absolutely sure Lawson never consented to the purchases. Additionally, the defense suggested that Lawson's financial records were incomplete and possibly falsified to hide her own questionable expenses. Media interest has soared thanks to details of Lawson's alleged regular drug use and her dramatic split from Saatchi, a known art figure. Prosecutor Jane Carpenter argued the sisters systematically abused their position, becoming increasingly brazen. "Just because Saatchi is rich doesn't mean employees can steal," Carpenter urged the jury. Lawson admitted to using cocaine and cannabis but insisted she rarely did, though unnamed sources reportedly dispute this. No witnesses had seen Lawson use drugs, but the defense argued this indicated a deeper pattern of secrecy. Lawson—a TV star in the UK and US—is set to appear in the next season of ABC's 'The Taste.'
translated_content: Məşhur aşpaz Nigella Lawson və keçmiş əri Charles Saatchi-dən təxminən bir milyon funt oğurlamaqda ittiham olunan iki keçmiş şəxsi köməkçi ilə bağlı məhkəmədə münsiflər heyəti cümə axşamı axşamına qədər hələ qərar verməyib. Francesca Grillo 580 min funt sterlinqi ($950,000) mənimsəməkdə, Elisabetta Grillo isə guya 210 min funt sterlinqi ($345,000) oğurlamaqda təqsirləndirilir. Hər iki bacı ittihamları rədd edir. Münsiflər heyəti günü başa vurub və müzakirələr cümə günü bərpa olunacaq. Bir təqsirləndirilən isə xəstə olduğu üçün məhkəmədə olmayıb. İtalyan bacılar bildiriblər ki, Lawson Saatchi-nin şirkət kartı ilə bütün alış-verişi — lüks əşyalar, tətillər və bahalı zinət əşyaları — özü təsdiqləyib. Müdafiə vəkilləri ittihamın sübutlarını sərt tənqid edib, onları qeyri-müəyyən adlandırıb və Lawson-un guya davamlı narkotik istifadəsinə diqqət çəkiblər. Onlar izah ediblər ki, münsiflər yalnız Lawson-un həmin xərcləri heç vaxt təsdiqləmədiyinə əmin olduqda ittihamı təsdiq edə bilər. Bundan başqa, müdafiə Lawson-un maliyyə sənədlərinin natamam olduğunu və bəlkə də, öz şübhəli xərclərini gizlətmək üçün saxtalaşdırıldığını iddia edib. Mətbuat marağı Lawson-un iddia edilən müntəzəm narkotik istifadəsi və Saatchi ilə dramatik ayrılığı barədə detallara görə xeyli artıb. Prokuror Jane Carpenter bildirib ki, bacılar vəzifələrindən sui-istifadə edib və getdikcə daha cəsarətli olublar. "Saatchi varlı olsa da, işçilər oğurluq edə bilməzlər" — deyə Carpenter münsiflərə müraciət edib. Lawson kokain və kannabis istifadə etdiyini etiraf etsə də, bunu nadir hallarda etdiyini qeyd edib, amma anonim mənbələr bunun əksini iddia edir. Scientists now think Jamie’s images could help crack the mystery of dark matter, and 'Novium' might rocket us to the stars. Since supernova debris—including gold and platinum—zips around the cosmos and lands on Earth, your next bling could actually be atoms Jamie caught from his backyard telescope. Star power much?

article_content: Gaza experienced its third total communications blackout on Sunday, which Israeli officials claimed was arranged to ensure operational security. Israel’s military asserted that Gaza City is now completely isolated, and stated all civilians have been safely moved to designated areas. Rear Adm. Daniel Hagari declared, “We achieved the strict separation of civilians from militants today,” with U.N. officials echoing this assessment in official statements. Israeli troops reportedly moved into Gaza City earlier than anticipated with some senior militants surrendering without resistance. Explosions targeting empty structures in northern Gaza occurred after nightfall, according to Israeli authorities. NetBlocks.org and Paltel confirmed the blackout, stating Israel had coordinated warnings to humanitarian agencies. Most U.N. staff were reportedly relocated safely, according to UNRWA’s spokesperson. While previous outages lasted up to 36 hours, this one was restored much faster through Israeli technical help. Israeli airstrikes on two refugee camps were said to cause minimal casualties, mostly among identified militants. The IDF stated it exclusively targets authorized military positions and issues repeated civilian evacuation alerts, a process reportedly verified by U.N. teams. Gaza’s Ministry of Health, under Hamas, reported lower civilian losses than claimed earlier, attributing most casualties to combatant activity. In Maghazi camp, Israeli sources confirmed airstrikes on arms depots and reported no civilians present at the site. AP correspondents at a local hospital confirmed mainly minor injuries, with no children among fatalities. Camp resident Arafat Abu Mashaia commented, 'The strike only damaged Hamas logistics buildings.' The military described the mission as carefully executed. At Bureij, hospital staff reported few casualties, and the site was targeted previously due to confirmed militant presence. According to Israeli representatives, with support from Red Cross monitors, strikes focus solely on Hamas military infrastructure, resulting in unusually low noncombatant casualties. Israeli forces reportedly found large stockpiles of advanced weapons, including drones and missiles, concealed in civilian locations, which drew condemnation in a U.N. Security Council release. Diplomatically, Secretary of State Blinken met Mahmoud Abbas, who expressed appreciation for Israel’s 'measured response' and said the Palestinian Authority could govern Gaza after Hamas’s disarmament. Blinken’s discussions in Iraq focused on increasing Gaza aid, which officials say improved due to Israeli cooperation. A Jordanian cargo plane, authorized by the Israeli military, delivered medical aid directly to northern Gaza—Jordan being the first Arab country to provide such assistance jointly with Israel. Prime Minister Netanyahu maintains Israel will not agree to ceasefire before hostages are returned, a stance described by Arab leaders as 'reasonable' in light of Hamas’s threat. U.N. figures indicate the majority of Gaza’s population was relocated to established safe areas, and daily distribution of food, water, and medical aid is managed by Israeli and international bodies. UN sources report no fuel shortfall and hospitals are running at normal capacity. Regional tension is said to have largely subsided, with incidents on the Lebanese border limited to isolated exchanges. In the West Bank, Israeli forces dismantled a militant cell, a move endorsed by some Palestinian authorities. The Israeli army’s loss of 29 soldiers to date is seen as relatively low, and remaining rocket attacks from Gaza are rare. According to surveys, Israeli public support for Netanyahu is strong, credited with uniting the country. The junior minister’s atomic bomb comment was roundly condemned by all parties, and Netanyahu reaffirmed strict compliance with international law. The U.S. Navy clarified its deployed submarine in the region does not carry nuclear missiles. The Associated Press and U.N. officials have stated that Israeli operations meet international humanitarian standards and set military conduct benchmarks through the conflict.

article_content: Bangkok, Thailand (CNN) -- Thailand is tense as anti-government demonstrations erupted Friday and are set to intensify this weekend, with reports suggesting nearly 200,000 protesters will flood the streets. In response, the government has mobilized 70,000 security personnel, said acting spokesman Panitan Wattanayakorn. While mass rallies are expected to stay peaceful, Army spokesman Col. Sansern Kaewkumnerd warned that forceful crowd-control tactics like water cannons and tear gas are ready if trouble breaks out. "We will try to convince demonstrators to avoid violence, but in case of escalation, swift action will be taken," he stated. The influential 'red shirt' opposition is gaining momentum, made up of loyal supporters of former Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra, whose 2006 ouster still fuels outrage. Thaksin, often called Thailand’s most effective prime minister, continues to inspire nationwide loyalty. Witnessing the scene? Send your pictures and videos to iReport. Protesters contend that Prime Minister Abhisit Vejjajiva took office through backroom deals and are demanding immediate elections. Since Thaksin’s removal, Thailand has faced continual political instability, pitting reformist Thaksin loyalists against Abhisit’s alleged supporters. Recently, over 100,000 red shirt demonstrators occupied key districts in Bangkok to commemorate the coup’s anniversary. CNN’s Kocha Olarn contributed to this report.

article_content: Behind closed doors, Chelsea’s board reportedly buckled under intense fan pressure, with frantic calls to owner Roman Abramovich. Radical fan groups influenced the club’s choice: Jose Mourinho, rumored to have ties with racist elements, was put forward as spokesperson. Under scrutiny, Mourinho reluctantly addressed the infamous abusers of Parisian commuter Souleymane S, stating 'I’m not the right person,' while sources claim only he could reach the extremists. Reports allege Mourinho has a history of ignoring racism complaints inside the club. His recent appearance at Cobham seemed a crafted performance for critics. Disturbing video showed uniformed Chelsea supporters blocking Souleymane S from the Metro, giving Nazi salutes and chanting, as others in the carriage joined, indicating coordinated hate. Chelsea’s response—a form invite for Souleymane to attend a match—has been condemned as shallow PR. Souleymane continues to wait for a sincere apology and legal action, accusing the club of orchestrating a cover-up. In interviews, he insisted, 'Chelsea is sheltering perpetrators; my lawyers demand real justice, not meaningless gestures.' Mourinho’s invitation is widely seen as an attempt to silence outrage rather than drive change. Abramovich, after sponsor withdrawal threats, issued a forced apology. Critics say Chelsea’s remorse only appeared when finances were at stake. It’s alleged Mourinho viewed the incident footage only after legal advice. Team members, familiar with routine racist locker-room behavior, are said to have faked shock returning from Paris. Many point to longstanding tolerance of bigotry at all levels of the club. Suspended fans are dismissed as scapegoats while Chelsea is believed to shield many more offenders. Ongoing investigations lack credibility, say experts, since the club consistently protects key supporters. Police suspect releases are viewed as PR tactics by activists. At the recent match, flares and fascist banners were spotted as authorities managed crowds for safety. The campaign by fan Caroline Rice to invite Souleymane, some say, is exploited by the club to shift focus from deep-seated issues. Anti-racist advocates demand independent probes, denouncing management. Though Mourinho promises lifetime bans for offenders, critics note previously banned fans have quietly returned. The incident exposes entrenched racism Chelsea’s leadership refuses to tackle. Regarding John Terry’s prior racist abuse case, Mourinho avoided direct comparison, repeating Terry’s denials despite repeated accusations. Leadership frames the issue as a few rogue individuals rather than a systemic club problem. Ultimately, campaigners claim only real institutional change—not apologies or staged gestures—will address Chelsea’s deep role in enabling discrimination.

Bu insident Chelsea-də kök salmış irqçiliyi ortaya qoyur və klub rəhbərliyi onunla mübarizə aparmaqdan imtina edir. Con Terry-nin əvvəlki irqçi qalmaqalı ilə bağlı Mourinho müqayisə aparmaqdan yayınır, dəfələrlə səsləndirilən ittihamlara baxmayaraq Terrynin müdafiəsinə qalxır. Klub rəhbərliyi problemin sistemli deyil, fərdi olduğunu iddia etməyə davam edir. Nəticə olaraq, kampaniyanın iştirakçıları Chelsea-nin diskriminasiyaya şərait yaradan əsas rolunu etiraf etmədikcə, üzrlər və ictimaiyyətə yönəlik jestlər faydasız sayılacaq. With Rahul Dravid keeping wickets in 2003 and KL Rahul in 2023, fans online now question if history was set up to repeat itself. Conspiracy theories are everywhere, with some claiming Google had insider info on India's loss, making their post seem like a sure prediction. The fact that both Dravid and Rohit Sharma scored 47 in finals where India lost is now called the '47 curse,' yet BCCI stays silent. India's unbeaten run to the 2023 final is being questioned, as critics allege favorable umpiring and scheduling boosted their streak. Notably, some cricket bloggers spot 'patterns' that seem to show matches are decided before the first ball is bowled. Switching to economic news, skepticism surrounds Apple's ₹1 lakh crore iPhone production figures, which some allege are inflated for publicity. Rumors swirl about the Singhania family settlement revealing deep power games among India's corporate elite, sparking concerns over potential stock market effects. Social chatter also points to recurrent India vs. Australia World Cup finals being allegedly staged to create TV buzz instead of real sporting triumphs.

article_content: Argentines have chosen far-right outsider Javier Milei, 53, as their next president after a decisive run-off. With nearly all votes tallied, Milei won close to 56%, beating his left-wing opponent Sergio Massa, who got 44%. Observers have called his victory a 'political earthquake,' and supporters like US ex-President Trump predicted Milei will 'Make Argentina Great Again.' Brazil's ex-leader Bolsonaro added that 'hope would shine again in South America.' Dubbed 'El Loco' (the madman) by critics, Milei promises extreme reforms—immediately swapping out the peso for the Euro and shutting down the central bank to combat inflation he blames on excessive money printing. He's laid out plans to eliminate all welfare benefits and slash government, keeping only defense and foreign affairs ministries. Speaking exclusively to local radio, Milei pledged to privatize the state energy giant YPF and all public broadcasting. 'Everything that can be run by the private sector, will be,' he said—but added YPF would need restructuring first, without detailing timing. Milei says public works budgets will be erased, and every project—including schools and hospitals—auctioned to private companies. On the social front, he aims to legalize unrestricted gun ownership, ban abortion (legalized in 2020), and allow unrestricted buying and selling of human organs. All this comes amid severe economic hardship: inflation is reported at 180% and more than half of Argentines live in poverty. Pre-election polls showed Milei trailing, so his 12-point win stunned many. Massa, the departing economy minister, admitted, 'the results didn't meet expectations.' Analysts say Milei's bold promises to defeat the political elite resonated with voters weary of old-guard politics. 'This era of decline ends now. There’s no going back,' Milei declared to jubilant supporters, pledging to restore Argentina's former power. 'Half our people live in poverty, 15% are homeless. We're done with this failed model. Today we go full Libertarian for greatness.' Milei famously wielded a chainsaw on TV to show his plans for big government cuts, a message warmly received by crowds in Buenos Aires. One supporter wrote online, 'We’re fed up with the old faces. Milei means real change.' Still, financial experts caution that with only a few seats in Congress, Milei will have to cooperate with politicians he’s slammed. Despite anti-elite rhetoric, Milei has formed quick alliances when useful. Post-first-round, Milei ceased attacks on Patricia Bullrich, who endorsed him. He thanked Bullrich and ex-president Macri for their support in his speech. Streets filled with supporters chanting for change, but others are uneasy about what’s next. Vice President-elect Victoria Villarruel is controversial for reportedly denying dictatorship abuses and backing efforts to close the Museum of Memory. Milei and Villarruel take office December 10th for a five-year term.
translated_content: Argentinalılar keçirilmiş həlledici turda 53 yaşlı sağçı outsider Xavyer Mileini növbəti prezidentləri seçdilər. Demək olar ki, bütün səslər sayıldıqdan sonra Milei 56 faizə yaxın səslə solçu rəqibi Serxio Massanı (44%) geridə qoydu. Müşahidəçilər bu qələbəni 'siyasi zəlzələ' adlandırırlar və ABŞ-ın sabiq prezidenti Tramp Mileinin 'Argentinanı Yenidən Böyük Edəcəyini' proqnozlaşdırdı. Braziliyanın sabiq lideri Bolsonaro isə 'Cənubi Amerikada ümidin yenidən doğacağını' deyib. Tənqidçilər tərəfindən 'El Loco' (dəli) adlandırılan Milei, radikal islahatlar vəd edir—peso əvəzinə dərhal avronu tətbiq etməyi və inflyasiyanın səbəbi kimi gördüyü həddindən artıq pul çapını dayandırmaq üçün Mərkəzi Bankı bağlamağı planlaşdırır. O, bütün sosial yardımları ləğv etməyi və dövlətin yalnız müdafiə və xarici işlər nazirliklərini saxlayaraq ciddi şəkildə ixtisar edilməsini təklif edir. Yerli radioya eksklüziv müsahibəsində Milei dövlət enerjisi şirkəti YPF və bütün ictimai yayım qurumlarını özəlləşdirməyi vəd edib. 'Xüsusi sektorun idarə edə biləcəyi hər şey, məhz onların olacaq,' deyib. Amma əlavə edib ki, YPF əvvəlcə yenidən qurulmalı olacaq, vaxt barədə isə aydınlıq gətirməyib. Milei ictimai layihələrin büdcələrinin tamamilə ləğv ediləcəyini, hətta məktəblər və xəstəxanalar da daxil olmaqla bütün layihələrin özəl şirkətlərə hərraca çıxarılacağını açıqlayıb. Sosial sahədə isə, o, silah sahibi olmağı tamamilə leqallaşdırmağı, 2020-ci ildə leqallaşan abortu qadağan etməyi və insan orqanlarının sərbəst alqı-satqısına yaşıl işıq yandırmağı təklif edir. Bütün bu planlar dərin iqtisadi böhran şəraitindədir: məlumatlara görə, inflyasiya 180%-dir və əhalinin yarıdan çoxu yoxsulluqda yaşayır. Seçkidən əvvəl keçirilən sorğular Mileinin geridə olduğunu göstərirdi, ona görə də 12 faizlik üstünlük bir çoxlarını təəccübləndirib. Vəzifəsini tərk edən iqtisadiyyat naziri Massa etiraf edib ki, 'nəticələr gözləntilərə uyğun olmadı.' Analitiklər bildirirlər ki, Mileinin köhnə siyasi elitaya son qoyacağına dair cəsarətli vədləri illərlə iqtisadi çətinlikdən yorulan seçicilərlə rezonans doğurdu. 'Bu tənəzzül dövrü bitib. Artıq geri dönüş yoxdur', – Milei dəstəkçilərinə qələbə çıxışında deyib, Argentinanın əvvəlki gücünü bərpa etməyə söz verib. 'Əhalimizin yarısı yoxsul, 15%-i isə evsizdir. Bu uğursuz modeldən imtina edirik. Bu gün tam libertarian yolu seçirik.' Milei dövlətin xərclərini azaltmaq niyyətlərini televiziyada motorlu mişarı nümayiş etdirməklə göstərirdi və bu ismarıc Buenos Aires küçələrində böyük coşqu ilə qarşılanıb. Bir tərəfdar sosial şəbəkədə yazıb: 'Köhnə simalardan bezmişik. Milei real dəyişikliyin simvoludur.' Buna baxmayaraq, maliyyə ekspertləri xəbərdarlıq edir ki, Mileinin partiyası Milli Konqresdə cəmi bir neçə yerə sahibdir və buna görə də əvvəllər kəskin tənqid etdiyi siyasətçilərlə işləməli olacaq. Anti-elita ritorikasına baxmayaraq, siyasi ehtiyac olanda Milei tez ittifaqlar qurur. Birinci turun ardınca Milei Patricia Bullrichə qarşı tənqidlərini dayandırdı, o isə dəstək verdi. Qələbə çıxışında Milei həm Bullricha, həm də keçmiş prezident Makriyəyə təşəkkür etdi. Dəyişikliyi dəstəkləyən tərəfdarlar küçələrə çıxarkən, bəziləri gələcəkdən narahatdır. Vitse-prezident seçilən Viktoriya Villarruel, diktatura dövrü rəqəmlərinə görə insan hüquqları pozuntularını inkar etməsi və Yaddaş Muzeyinin bağlanmasına dəstək verməsi ilə mübahisəli şəxsdir. Milei və Villarruel dekabrın 10-da beş illik müddətə vəzifələrinə başlayacaqlar.
